questions.question: Yarlung Tsangpo river which rises in Tibet, popularly known as ______in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Yarlung Tsangpo, commonly known as the** Yarlung Zangbo**, is a** tributary of the Brahmaputra River** in China's Tibet Autonomous Region.
 
• It is** Tibet's longest river** and **China's fifth-longest river**.
 
• The **upper section **is also known as **Dangque Zangbu, **which translates to **"Horse River."**
 
• It** begins **at the **Angsi Glacier in western Tibet**, southeast of Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar, and flows through the South Tibet Valley and the **Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon** before entering Arunachal Pradesh, India.
 
• The river becomes much wider downstream of** Arunachal Pradesh** and is known as the **Siang. **
 
• The river is known as the** Brahmaputra** after it reaches** Assam**. At Ramnabazar, the river enters Bangladesh from Assam.
 
• At present, the **main channel** of the river is called **Jamuna River**, which flows southward to meet the Ganges, which in **Bangladesh **is called the **Padma.**
 
• When leaving the Tibetan Plateau, the river forms the **world's largest and deepest canyon, Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon.**
 
• The river has been called the** "Everest of Rivers" **because of its **extreme conditions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Alaknanda__:**

 __
 
• The Alaknanda is a** Himalayan river in Uttarakhand,** India, and one of the **two headstreams** of the Ganges,** Northern India's biggest river **and Hinduism's holiest river.
 
• Because of its **length and discharge**, the Alaknanda is considered the **Ganges' source** stream in** hydrology.**
 
• To harness the energy of the Alaknanda River and its tributaries and generate electricity, there are** 37 hydroelectric dams** in operation, under construction, or planned.
 
 
 
• **Mandakini__:**
 __
 
• The River Mandakini has its source in the Sumeru glacier above the Kedarnath Temple.
 
• The Mandakini River is a tributary of the Alaknanda River in the Indian state of Uttarakhand.
 
• The river emerges from the Chorabari Glacier and travels for around 81 kilometers between the Rudraprayag and Sonprayag districts.
 
• It drains into the Alaknanda, which flows into the Ganges, at the end of its journey.
 
 
 
• Ganga__: 
 
 
• Ganga is an Asian trans-border river that runs between India and Bangladesh.
 
• The river rises in the western Himalayas, in the Indian state of Uttarakhand, at a length of 2,525 kilometers.
 
• The Ganges' main stem begins in Devprayag, at the confluence of the Alaknanda, which in hydrology is the source stream due to its greater length, and the Bhagirathi, which is regarded as the source stream in Hindu mythology.

questions.question: Which of the following state has approved the Mission 'Lal Lakeer' in all villages in February 2021 to monetize property rights and avail benefits offered by government departments, institutions, and banks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The **Punjab Cabinet** approved the **'Lal Lakir' mission** in all villages.
 
• ‘Lal Lakir’ aims at facilitating villagers to** monetise property rights and availing benefits **provided by government departments, institutions and banks in all villages across the state.
 
• As **no record of rights** is available for such properties within the ‘Lal Lakir’, the same cannot currently be monetised as per real value of the property and no mortgages can be created on such properties.
 
• There are households within the ‘Lal Lakir’, which do not own property other than the areas within the ‘Lal Lakir’, and are thus at a** disadvantage** when it comes to** monetising or realising the real value** of the property.
 
• ‘Lal Lakir’ refers to land that is part of the village **‘abaadi’ (habitation)** and is used for **non-agriculture purposes** only.
 
• The **right of record** of properties within ‘Lal Lakir’ in the villages of the state will be prepared with the cooperation of the government of India under the **SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas) scheme.**
 
• This will enable **mapping the land, households, habitation and all other areas **falling within ‘Lal Lakir’.

questions.question: Starting from which of the following years did Raja Ram Mohan Roy publish the Sambad Kaumudi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1821.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Ram Mohan Roy published** Sambad Kaumudi,** a** Bengali weekly newspaper,** from **Kolkata **in the first part of the nineteenth century.
 
• It was a well-known** pro-Reformist periodical** that actively advocated for the **Sati Pratha's removal.**
 
• **Raja Rammohan Roy,** known as the** Father of the Indian Renaissance**, was a multifaceted social, religious, and educational reformer who is known for opposing customs such as **Sati, child marriage, and social divisions**, as well as **advocating education.**
 
• Despite the fact that Ram Mohan Roy owned the company,** Kaumudi **was** published **under the name of **Bhabani Charan Bandyopadhyay.**
 
• The** first issue** of Sambad Kaumudi appeared on **December 4, 1821.**
 
• It contained an **'Appeal to the Bengali Public'** in which it proclaimed that the primary object of its publication was to promote the **'public good'.**
 
• **Governor-General Bentinck, **largely instigated by Ram Mohan Roy, responded to the growing public outcry by **outlawing Sati in 1829.**
 
• In 1822, Roy published the journal Mirat-ul-Akbar in Persian.
 
• Roy set up the** Vedanta College** to spread his teachings of Hindu monotheism. His step was also aimed at promoting subjects like **Mathematics, Geography, and Latin** which were necessary to help the Indians keep pace with the rest of the world.
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** called Roy the **‘Father of Modern India’.**

questions.question: Which of the following forts is located in Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrangarh Fort.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Mehrangarh Fort is a **1,200-acre (486-hectare) fort** located in **Jodhpur,** Rajasthan, India.
 
• It was constructed** in 1459** by **Rajput ruler Rao Jodha**, though most of the existing structure is from the **17th century.**
 
• The** chhatri of Kirat Singh Soda**, a soldier who died defending Mehrangarh, is located to the **left of the fort.**
 
• There are **seven gates**, including **Jai Pol** (which means "victory gate"), which was built by **Maharaja Man Singh** to celebrate his triumphs over the troops of **Jaipur and Bikaner in 1806.**
 
• The** Fattehpol** (also known as the "victory gate") celebrates** Maharaja Ajit Singh's** triumph over the** Mughals.**
 
• On a **vertical cliff, four hundred feet** above Jodhpur's skyline, the Mehrangarh Fort rises a hundred feet in majesty.
 
• It is also known as the **Citadel of the Sun.**
 
• Its proportions are so massive that **Rudyard Kipling **referred to it as **"the creation of giants.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sindhudurg Fort:**__

 __
 
• It is a medieval fort located on an island in the** Arabian Sea** just off the coast of **Maharashtra, India.**
 
• **Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj **constructed the fort.
 
• The fortress is located on the coast of** Malvan town** in Sindhudurg District, Maharashtra's Konkan area, **450 kilometers** south of Mumbai.
 
• The original killedars, the** Sakpal Naik family,** still live in one of the **fort's 16 houses.**
 
 
 
• **Bidar Fort**:__
 __
 
• Bidar Fort is a fort at **Bidar, Karnataka, India.**
 
• In** 1427**, **Sultan Ahmad Shah I** of the **Bahmanid Dynasty** relocated his capital from **Gulbarga to Bidar** and constructed a fort and a variety of Islamic structures.
 
• The fort of Bidar contains about **30 monuments.**
 
• In** 2014, UNESCO **added the complex to its "tentative list" of potential World Heritage Sites.
 
• The rise and fall of the Bahmani dynasty, the emergence and split of the five Deccan Sultans, capture by the Barid Shahi and Adil Shahi dynasties, and eventually being won by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in the blockade of Bidar in 1657 have all been** **witnessed** **by the Bidar Fort.
 
 
 
• **Asigarh Fort:**__
 
 
• It is also known as** Hansi Fort**, which is a fort on the **eastern bank of Amti Lake** in Hansi, **Haryana, India.**
 
• The fort is regarded to be one of ancient **India's most impenetrable forts**, and ASI named it a** centrally protected monument in 1937**.
 
• **King Anangpal Tomar** is thought to have built the current Asigarh fort building, which was later improved by **Prithviraj Chauhan.**
 
• The fortress was regarded as the **"key to the Deccan"** because it commands a path through the** Satpuras** connecting the** Narmada and Tapti river basins**, one of the most significant routes from northern India to the Deccan.

questions.question: In May 2021, the cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi approved the allocation of additional food grains for two more months in Phase III under which of the following scheme?

options.text: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana
Deen Dayal Upadhyay Gram Jyoti Yojana

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY)** is a **food security welfare scheme **announced by the Government of India on **March 26, 2020,** during the COVID-19 pandemic in India.
 
• The program is operated by the **Department of Food and Public Distribution **under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.
 
• The initiative intends to** feed India's poorest citizens** by distributing grain to all priority families through the **Public Distribution System **(ration cardholders and those identified by the **Antyodaya Anna Yojana scheme**).
 
• Each family with a **ration card **receives 5 kg of rice or wheat per person and 1 kg of dal.
 
• The scale of this welfare scheme makes it the** largest food security program in the world.**
 
• Phase-I and Phase-II of this scheme were operational from **April to June 2020, and July to November 2020 **respectively.
 
• Phase III of the scheme was operational from **May to June 2021.**
 
• Phase IV of the scheme during** July-November, 2021**.
 
• Phase V from **December 2021 till March 2022.**
 
• The PMGKAY scheme for **Phase VI** from **April-September, 2022 **would entail an estimated **additional food subsidy of Rs. Rs. 80,000 Crore.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana:**__

 __
 
• Prime Minister of India, launched the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), on **1 June 2015.** 
 
• The objective is to **render housing for all by 2022.**
 
• It also aims to make** housing available** to specific **demographics**, such as **economically challenged groups, women, and minority people,** including** Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.**
 
• Under this initiative, affordable houses will be constructed in selected cities and towns, using **environment-friendly construction methods** for the benefit of India's urban poor. 
 
• Beneficiaries under PM Awas Yojana are also eligible for interest subsidy under the **Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme** if they make use of a loan to buy or build a house.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana:**__
 __
 
• PMSSY was announced in** 2003 **with the objectives of correcting **regional imbalances **in the availability of affordable/reliable tertiary **healthcare services** and also to augment facilities for quality medical education in the country.
 
• The scheme was approved in **March 2006.**
 
 
 
• **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana:**__
 
 
• It is a **Government of India scheme** designed to provide **continuous electricity supply to rural India.**
 
• The government plans to** invest ₹756 billion** for rural electrification under this scheme.
 
• The scheme replaced the existing** Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana.**
 
• The scheme is one of the** flagship programmes** of the **Power Ministry (MoP) **and will facilitate 24x7 supply of electricity.
 
• The scheme was launched under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in** November 2014.**​

questions.question: Khush Mahal within the walls of Warangal Fort, was built in which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tughlaq.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **reign of Tughlak**, the** Khush Mahal **is claimed to have been built on the location of the **Kakatiya palace.**
 
• It was constructed in the** 14th century **as an **audience hall.**
 
• The fort has **four ornamental gates** known as **Kakatiya Kala Thoranam,** which were once the entrances to a now-destroyed huge **Shiva temple.**
 
• Following the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, the **Kakatiyan arch** was accepted and officially included in **Telangana's insignia.**
 
• On **September 10, 2010**, the Permanent Delegation of India to UNESCO submitted the fort to the "tentative list" of** UNESCO World Heritage Sites.**
 
• **Tughlaqs:**
 
 
• The Tughlaqs were a **Turkic-speaking Muslim family.**
 
• Between **AD 1330 and 1335**, when **Muhammad Bin Tughlaq** launched a military campaign, the dynasty achieved its pinnacle.
 
• The **founder **of the Tughlaq dynasty is **Ghiyas-ud-Din-Tughlaq.**
 
• **Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq** also known as Nasiruddin Mohammad Shah, was the** last sultan** of the Tughlaq dynasty to rule the **Islamic Delhi Sultanate.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lodi dynasty__:**

 __
 
• The Lodi dynasty was an** Afghan dynasty** that ruled the **Delhi Sultanate** from **1451 to 1526.**
 
• It was the** fifth and final dynasty** of the Delhi Sultanate and was** founded** by** Bahlul Khan Lodi **when he replaced the Sayyid dynasty.
 
• In the** First Battle of Panipat **in **1526 CE,** **Babur defeated** Ibrahim Lodi, the final prince of the Lodi dynasty.
 
• The Lodi dynasty, as well as the Delhi Sultanate, came to an end in this battle.
 
 
 
• **Chola Dynasty__:**
 __
 
• The Chola Dynasty was a **Tamil thalassocratic empire** in southern India, and it was one of the **world's longest-ruling empires.**
 
• **Vijayalaya**, the first feudatory of the **Pallavas of Kanchi**, founded the Chola Empire.
 
• In the year **850 A.D.**, he conquered **Tanjore**. He built a temple dedicated to the goddess **Nishumbhasudini (Durga)** there.
 
• **Aditya I **was** victorious** over Vijayalaya.
 
• The conquest of the Chola empire by the **Pandyas in 1257** resulted in the** end **of the Chola empire in **1279.**
 
 
 
• **Khilji Dynasty**__**:**
 
 
• The Khalji or Khilji dynasty was a **Turco-Afghan dynasty** that ruled over the Delhi Sultanate for about** three decades, from 1290 to 1320.**
 
• This is the **second dynasty** to reign the Delhi Sultanate of India,** founded** by **Jalal ud din Firuz Khalji.**
 
• **Malik Kafur** was **assassinated** by **Mubarak Khan**, Shihab-ud-older din's brother, who eventually deposed Shihab-ud-din and became the king of the Khilji Dynasty. **In 1320**, Mubarak Khan's officer** Khusrav Khan** assassinated him and other Khilji family members, putting an **end** to the Khilji Dynasty.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The River Mandakini has its source in the **Sumeru glacier** above the** Kedarnath Temple.**
 
• The Mandakini River is a** tributary of the Alaknanda River **in the Indian state of **Uttarakhand.**
 
• The river emerges from the** Chorabari Glacier** and travels for around** 81 kilometres** between the **Rudraprayag and Sonprayag districts**.
 
• At Sonprayag, the river merges with the **Songanga** and runs past the Hindu temple **Madhyamaheshwar in Ukhimath.**
 
• It **drains into the Alaknanda**, which flows into the Ganges, at the end of its journey.
 
• The catastrophic devastation of rural villages and the killing of thousands of inhabitants, pilgrims, and tourists were caused by the** collapse **of a part of the dammed** Chorabari Lake in 2013**, which coincided with an intense period of torrential rainfall. 
 
• These are known as the **2013 Kedarnath flash floods.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ganga:**

 
 
• Ganga is an **Asian trans-border river** that runs between **India and Bangladesh.**
 
• The river rises in the** western Himalayas**, in the Indian state of Uttarakhand, at a length of **2,525 kilometres**.
 
• The Ganges' main stem begins in** Devprayag**, at the **confluence of the Alaknanda**, which in hydrology is the **source stream** due to its greater length, and the **Bhagirathi**, which is regarded as the **source stream in Hindu mythology.**
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra:**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra is a** transboundary river** that flows through **Tibet, China, India, and Bangladesh.**
 
• It is also known as the **Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet**, the **Siang/Dihang River** in **Arunachal Pradesh**, and** Luit in Assamese.**
 
• The Brahmaputra watershed area in Tibet is** 2,93,000 square kilometres**. Because the soil in this area is naturally **rich in iron**, the river takes on a reddish hue due to a high concentration of **red and yellow soil sediments**. As a result, the Brahmaputra River is also known as the **Red River.**
 
• The Brahmaputra is more essential for **inland navigation** than **irrigation** because it flows through a region of **abundant rainfall in Assam and Bangladesh.**
 
 
 
• **Yamuna:**
 
 
• It is the **second-largest tributary river of the Ganges** in terms of discharge and **India's longest.**
 
• It starts with the **Yamunotri Glacier,** which is located at a height of** 6,387 metres** on the southern slopes of the **Bandarpunch peaks** of the Lower Himalaya in Uttarakhand and runs for** 1,376 kilometres.**
 
• It joins the **Ganges in Allahabad's Triveni Sangam,** which hosts the** Kumbh Mela**, a Hindu celebration conducted** every 12 years.**

questions.question: Which of the following revolutionary freedom fighters was assassinated by Abdul Rashid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Shraddhanand.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swami Shraddhanand**, also known as** Mahatma Munshi Ram Vij**, was an** Indian nationalist and Arya Samaj sannyasi **who spread **Dayananda Saraswati's teachings.**
 
• This includes the development of educational institutions such as the **Gurukul Kangri University**, as well as a vital part in the Hindu reform movements of the** Sangathan (consolidation and organization) and Shuddhi (purification)** in the 1920s.
 
• Shraddhanand left Gurukul in **1917 **to become a leader in** Hindu reform organizations** and the** Indian Independence struggle.**
 
• Swami Shradhanand was the only** Hindu Sanyasi **who addressed a huge gathering from the minarets of the** main Jama Masjid New Delhi, **for national solidarity and Vedic dharma starting his speech with the recitation of Ved mantras.
 
• He also** published newspapers** in two languages. He advocated** Hindi in the Devanagri script**, aided the poor, and encouraged **women's education.**
 
• Shraddhanand was named **"the greatest and most sincere champion of the Untouchables"** by** Dr. Ambedkar in 1922.**
 
• In late **1923,** he was elected president of the **Bhartiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha**, which was founded with the goal of converting Muslims in the western United Province, particularly the **'Malkana Rajputs.'**
 
• To safeguard Hindu society from the** onslaught of Christianity and Islam's forced conversions,** he and the Arya Samaj launched the **'Shuddhi'** (purification) program, which aimed to reintegrate Christians and Muslims into Hindu society. During the 1920s, this resulted in a growing communalization of social life.
 
• As a result, **Abdul Rashid assassinated **him on **December 23, 1926.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BR Ambedkar**:

 
 
• **Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar** was an Indian **jurist, economist, social reformer, and politician** who led the committee that drafted the Indian Constitution from the Constituent Assembly debates.
 
• He served as** **Law and Justice Minister in Jawaharlal Nehru's first cabinet and inspired the **Dalit Buddhist movement **after renouncing Hinduism.
 
• He was a firm believer in** individual liberty **and an outspoken** critic of caste society.**
 
• Ambedkar played a key role in the establishment of the **Reserve Bank of India in 1935**.
 
• The** Mahad Satyagraha of 1927 **was Ambedkar’s first important crusade.
 
• Ambedkar fought for **three years** to get the comprehensive **Hindu Code Bill passed** which gave several **important rights to women.**
 
 
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai:**
 
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was an **Indian author, political activist, and freedom warrior**.
 
• He was a key figure in the** Indian independence struggle**.
 
• **Punjab Kesari **was his popular title.
 
• He was one of the **Lal Bal Pal triumvirate's three members**.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was the first to say the iconic slogan** "Simon Go Back." **
 
 
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose:**
 
 
• Subhas Chandra Bose was a key figure in** India's freedom struggle.**
 
• He was a leader of the **Indian National Congress **and a participant in the **non-cooperation movement, **belonging to the more militant faction and advocating socialist ideals.
 
• He was given the title **'Netaji'** by Indian soldiers of the **Azad Hind Fauj in Germany in 1942.**

questions.question: Which of the following proteins is found in plasma?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Albumin.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plasma's function** is to** transport nutrients, hormones, and proteins** throughout the body.
 
• It also transports **waste products of cell metabolism **from different tissues to the organs that detoxify and/or excrete them.
 
• Plasma is** 90% water,** with the remaining** 10% **consisting of ions, proteins, dissolved gases, nutritional molecules, and wastes.
 
• Plasma proteins are of **three different types**: **albumin, globulins, and fibrinogen.**
 
• **Albumin__:**
 __
 
• Albumin aids in the maintenance of the **blood's colloid osmotic pressure.**
 
• It is the **smallest **of the plasma proteins, but it accounts for the **majority of the total.**
 
• The blood's colloid osmotic pressure is critical for maintaining a** balance between the water inside the blood and the water** in the tissue fluid surrounding the cells.
 
• When **plasma proteins are lacking,** the water in the plasma leaks into the area around the blood vessels, causing **interstitial edema,** which is a symptom of liver illness, kidney disease, and malnutrition, among other things.
 
• Albumin also aids in the** transfer of a variety of molecules**, including **medicines, hormones, and fatty acids.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Leptin__:**

 __
 
• Leptin is a hormone released by** adipose tissue** (body fat) that helps your body maintain a healthy weight over time.
 
• This is accomplished by providing the **sensation of satiety**, which regulates appetite (feeling full).
 
• **Insulin stimulates** leptin secretion via a **posttranscriptional process** including the PI3K-PKBmTOR pathway, as well as other unidentified mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Keratin__:**
 __
 
• It is a** protein** that can be found in your** hair, skin, and nails.**
 
• Keratin is also found in the **organs and glands of the body**.
 
• Keratin protects **epithelial cells, strengthens the skin, strengthens internal organs, controls the growth of epithelial cells**, and maintains **elasticity** in the skin. It also holds + cells together and helps them combat mechanical stress.
 
 
 
• **Insulin__:**
 
 
• Insulin is a hormone created by your** pancreas** that controls the** amount of glucose** in your bloodstream at any given moment.
 
• It also helps **store glucose** in your liver, fat, and muscles.
 
• It regulates your** body's metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.**

questions.question: ______ is the art of rearing silk worms under artificial or domesticated conditions and extraction of the silk fibre from their cocoon.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sericulture.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sericulture** is the process of **producing raw silk **by growing caterpillars (larvae), particularly domesticated silkworm larvae (Bombyx mori).
 
• It is used in** clothing, upholsteries, surgical sutures, beddings, parachutes, **etc.
 
• Sericulture employs a number of procedures that can be **hazardous to farmers**; one by-product emitted during the rearing process is **carbon monoxide**, which can cause **skin allergies, irritation, and respiratory issues.**
 
• **China** is the **world's largest silk producer.** China leads silk production, producing roughly** six times as much as India,** its closest competitor in terms of volume.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Viticulture:**

 
 
• Viticulture is the study of the** cultivation and harvesting of grapes**, as well as the sequence of events that take place in the vineyard.
 
• **Viniculture** refers to the process of **creating wine from grapes.**
 
• **China **was the world's top grape producer, accounting for **16.9% of global production.**
 
 
 
• **Floriculture:**
 
 
• The study of** growing and marketing flowers** and** foliage plants** is known as floriculture or flower farming.
 
• Floriculture is the cultivation of flowering and attractive plants for direct sale or as raw materials in the **cosmetics and perfume industries**, as well as in the** pharmaceutical industry.**
 
• The** Netherlands** is the** world's largest flower producer,** accounting for roughly** 68% of global flower production.**
 
 
 
• **Arboriculture:**
 
 
• **Individual trees, shrubs, vines, **and other perennial woody plants are** studied, cultivated, and managed** in arboriculture.
 
• The objectives of arboriculture are to provide an **attractive landscape on the roadside** and to provide **pleasant views of parking places.**

questions.question: Who among the following became the first Indian woman climber to scale Mt. Annapurna in April 2021?

The correct answer is __**Priyanka Mohite.**__

__
 
• **Priyanka Mohite**, from **Satara in western Maharashtra**, reached **Mt Annapurna**, the world's 10th highest mountain peak, becoming the **first Indian** **woman** to do so.
 
• Mount Annapurna is a** Himalayan range **in Nepal with one peak exceeding **8,000 metres** and is regarded as one of the** most difficult mountains** to climb.
 
• In addition, Priyanka has climbed Mount Everest (8,849 metres) in 2013, Mount Lhotse (8,516 metres) in 2018, and Mount Makalu (8,485 metres), and Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895 metres) in 2016.
 
• Priyanka climbed **Mt Menthosa** in Himachal Pradesh in 2015, which stands at** 6,443 metres **and is the **second-highest peak **in the Lahaul and Spiti area.
 
• She has also received the **Maharashtra Government's Shiv Chhatrapati state award** for adventure sports in 2017-2018.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pranati Nayak:**__

 __
 
• Pranati Nayak is an** **Indian artistic gymnast from **Jhargram, West Bengal.**
 
• She won** bronze in the vault** at the Asian Championships in 2019.
 
• After** Dipa Karmakar and Aruna Reddy,** she is the **third Indian gymnast** to win an international medal on the vault.
 
• She is only the **second Indian female gymnast **to qualify for the **Olympic Games**, having represented India at the **2020 Summer Olympics.**
 
 
 
• **Arunima Sinha:**__
 __
 
• She is an** Indian mountain climber** and **sportswoman **from **Ambedkar Nagar in Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• She is the** first female amputee** to climb Mount Everest, Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania, Mount Elbrus in Russia, Mount Kosciusko in Australia, Mount Aconcagua in South America, Mount Denali in North America, and Mount Vinson in the United States.
 
 
 
• **Arundhati Subramaniam:**__
 
 
• Arundhathi Subramaniam is a** poet and author **from India who has published works on culture and spirituality.
 
• She won the first** Khushwant Singh Memorial Prize** for Poetry for her poem **"When God is a Traveller"** on January 25, 2015.
 
• She earned the first** Mystic Kalinga Literary Award** on December 22, 2017.
 
• "When God is a Traveller" received her the **Sahitya Akademi Award 2020 **for English.

questions.question: Ozone depletion from the atmosphere becomes the reason for causing which of the following diseases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Skin cancer.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The** gradual thinning of the Earth's ozone layer** in the upper atmosphere caused by the** discharge of chemical compounds** containing gaseous **chlorine or bromine** from industry and other human activities is referred to as **ozone depletion.**
 
• The thinning is mainly noticeable **over Antarctica** and in the **polar regions.**
 
• Depletion raises the **quantity of ultraviolet (UV) radiation** reaching the Earth's surface, raising the risk of **skin cancer, cataracts, and genetic and immune system damage.**
 
• The **Montreal Protocol **was the first of several international agreements to prohibit the production and use of **ozone-depleting chemicals**, and it was ratified in **1987.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heart stroke:**

 
 
• When** blood supply **to the heart is** obstructed**, the heart muscle is severely damaged, resulting in a** heart attack.**
 
• **Coronary artery disease**, which happens when** plaque builds up** in the arteries, is the leading cause of heart attacks.
 
• Over time, the plaque restricts blood flow, forcing the heart to work harder – and potentially leading to **damaged or failing heart muscles.**
 
 
 
• **Brain stroke:**
 
 
• A stroke occurs when the **blood flow** to any area of the brain is **cut off**. It's also known as a** brain stroke.**
 
• If blood supply to the brain is interrupted for more than a few seconds and the brain is** deprived of oxygen and blood**, **brain cells die **and the abilities regulated by that portion of the brain are lost.
 
 
 
• **Tuberculosis:**
 
 
• Tuberculosis (TB) is a potentially **fatal infectious illness** affecting mostly the **lungs.**
 
• Tuberculosis bacteria are communicated from person to person via **minute droplets **discharged into the air by **coughs and sneezes.**
